newsitem.title: CONGO: Mediators agree Brazzaville peace blueprint.
newsitem.headline: Mediators agree Brazzaville peace blueprint.

text.p: A mediation committee in the battered capital of the former French colony of Congo agreed a peace blueprint on Friday, envisaging assembly of fighters and mixed patrols, a spokesman for the city's mayor said.

Edmond Munungi, spokesman for Mayor Bernard Kolelas, told Reuters that under the seven-point plan the patrols with representatives from all sides would be under the authority of the mediation committee.
"Both sides have representatives on the committee so we hope this will be respected," he said.
The bloody standoff between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor, former Marxist military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, dates back to June 5.
The fighting began after the army surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home as part of a crackdown on private militias and unauthorised arms in the runup to a July 27 election.

Supporters of Kolelas, runner-up to Lissouba in a 1992 presidential election, were in the thick of fighting which killed at least 2,000 people after disputed parliamentary elections in 1993. This time they stayed out of the conflict.
Munungi said the blueprint envisaged a progressive easing of an overnight curfew, which in theory begins at 7 p.m..

It also envisaged non-governmental organisations and the Red Cross having free access to clean up dead bodies, the restoration of telephone links and the progressive lifting of barricades on all roads.

The city was calmer on Friday than at any time during the standoff but it was not clear whether a truce had started to take hold. Lissouba and Sassou Nguesso both told their forces to cease fire on Wednesday. Fierce clashes followed on Thursday.
